{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfgB5wNHoec5vFeiimkyg","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've parallelized the benchmark with MPI, OpenMP and CUDA. Only `floydwarshall.cpp` and `CMakeLists.txt` changed, and the executable is still `floydwarshall`. On every size I tested, the distance matrix is bit-identical to the original (same `-r` hash, `-v` passes). That covers sizes 1, 7, 100, 512, 1000 and 2049, run with 1 to 5 ranks, including sizes that aren't a multiple of the tile size.\n\n**Performance** (4× RTX 3090, one node):\n\n| n | original (serial CPU) | 1 GPU | 4 GPUs |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 2049 | 9.4 s | — | — |\n| 8192 | — | 269 ms | 141 ms |\n| 16384 | — | 1851 ms | ~700 ms (~6.3 TOPS) |\n| 24576 | — | 6.0 s | 1.97 s (~7.5 TOPS) |\n\nGoing from 1 to 4 GPUs gives about 2.6× at n=16384 and about 3× at n=24576. Scaling improves as the problem gets bigger.\n\n**How it works:**\n- **CUDA:** the standard tiled (\"blocked\") form of Floyd-Warshall with 64×64 tiles. For each block of pivot nodes it updates the pivot tile, then the pivot's row and column, then all other tiles. That last step is the bulk of the work and each thread handles 16 entries. The path matrix is still computed on the GPUs, as in the original.\n- **MPI:** each rank owns a band of rows, one GPU per rank (assigned by node-local rank). Rank 0 builds the input with the same seeded random sequence and sends each rank its rows, then collects the result at the end.\n  - Each round, the owner of the next pivot row computes it early. Its broadcast then runs while the GPUs work on the current round.\n  - This MPI build can't send GPU memory directly, and a plain host broadcast only reached ~2 GB/s. So ranks on the same node share the pivot row through an MPI-3 shared-memory buffer, with one broadcast per node between nodes. Setups where nodes have different numbers of ranks fall back to a plain `MPI_Bcast`. That fallback was tested; the multi-node path couldn't be, since only one node is available here.\n- **OpenMP:** host-side copying (padding the input, unpacking the result). Generating the random input stays serial so the sequence is exactly the same as before.\n- **CMake:** builds the `.cpp` as CUDA with the GPU architecture auto-detected, and links MPI, OpenMP and the CUDA runtime. No new dependencies.\n\n**Things to know:**\n- **Timer scope:** \"Computation time\" covers copying to the GPUs, the computation with all its communication, and copying back to host memory. It doesn't include sending the input out from rank 0 or gathering the result back. I treated those like the original's initialization and output. Including them would add roughly 0.4 s at n=16384, mostly the result gather.\n- **Path matrix:** the distances match exactly. The path matrix isn't printed, and because the tiled version applies updates in a different order, some entries may record a different (still valid) intermediate node than the serial loop would.\n- Run with `mpirun -np <GPUs per node × nodes> ./floydwarshall -n N`. It also works without `mpirun` as a single rank.\n- I tried a version of the main kernel using wider shared-memory loads.
